- addresses, invoice numbers or statuses belonging to the second sandbox customer appear in no reply, context dump or log line of the verified session

- reading any sandbox order that the verified session does not own

Substituted boundary: the external adapter (in-memory for offline, approved sandbox for live). Frozen clock 2026-01-15T10:00:00Z; all waits are condition/deadline waits on the engine's virtual clock, never sleep. ### `E2E-LIVE-CART` - PILOT-02 + TC-E2E-007: cart recovery with floor-price guard and consent suppression (approved sandbox)

**Provenance**

- `PILOT-02` - Cart recovery: abandoned cart, customer context, eligibility, recommendation, message, conversion, order, attribution (SRS section 21)
- `TC-E2E-007` - A customer without matching consent is suppressed (SRS section 22)
- `SAL-04` - Cart Recovery Agent: detect abandoned cart, check customer, consent, stock, price and suppression rules, choose channel, act and measure conversion (SRS section 7)
- `SAL-05` - Reorder/Replenishment Agent: buying-cycle analysis, and no send when marketing is refused, product discontinued, stock unsuitable, recent repurchase or suppressed (SRS section 7)
- `FR-SAL-002` - Price and stock must come from authoritative data sources and must never be inferred (SRS section 7 (MUST))
- `FR-SAL-003` - Every recommendation carries customer, product, reason, evidence, eligibility, confidence and expected outcome (SRS section 7 (MUST))
- `BR-002` - AI must not change price or discount outside policy (SRS section 13 (MUST))
- `BR-004` - No marketing send without the matching customer consent (SRS section 13 (MUST))
- `BR-005` - An action with an external effect requires a unique execution ID (SRS section 13 (MUST))
- `BR-006` - Retry must not create a duplicate action (SRS section 13 (MUST))
- `NFR-003` - Idempotency: repeating the same execution request must not create a second unintended transaction (SRS section 19 (MUST))
- `NFR-008` - Failure safety: when price, stock, authority or consent cannot be verified the system fails closed (SRS section 19 (MUST))
- `SRS-11` - Skill System: skill contract fields including validation, retry, timeout, audit and test cases (SRS section 11)

**Real-life risk.** An abandoned-cart reminder reaches a customer who opted out, or is sent with a discount below the owner-approved floor — either way the company either harasses a customer or sells at a loss because the recovery message bypassed the policy guards.

**Inputs** (synthetic test configuration, never production policy)

```json
{
  "tenant_id": "LIVE_TENANT_ID",
  "customer_id": "LIVE_CUSTOMER_A_SANDBOX_ID",
  "cart_id": "sandbox cart created for this run",
  "channel": "EMAIL",
  "effect_key": "EK-E2E-LIVE-CART-<run_id>",
  "sandbox_recipient": "approved test mailbox only",
  "consent_check": "read live from the sandbox consent store at send time",
  "p_floor_source": "sandbox pricing service verdict for the sandbox SKU"
}
```

**Steps**

| # | Action | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Create and abandon the sandbox cart | the sandbox commerce API returns a cart owned by the sandbox customer and the abandonment condition fires from the scheduler, not from a sleep |
| 2 | Attempt the below-floor sandbox offer | the sandbox pricing service rejects the reduced price, no discounted quote is issued, and the sandbox provider test sink logs 0 sends for that attempt |
| 3 | Send the in-policy sandbox reminder | exactly one sandbox message is dispatched for the effect_key, recipient_count is 1 and the consent row is re-read at send time |
| 4 | Replay the abandonment on the sandbox | the reserve outcome is REPLAY with the stored receipt and the sandbox provider records exactly one message for the effect_key |
| 5 | Probe the suppression path on the sandbox | the second sandbox identity without consent is suppressed with ERR_CONSENT_SUPPRESSED and the provider test sink shows 0 calls for it — the provider test sink is the oracle for every denied or refused step: its call log for the run stays empty, no provider id is manufactured for the attempt, and the audit entry records the refusal instead |
| 6 | Observe recovery and pick up the receipts | the sandbox order/response script advances the outcome, and the provider receipt, reservation row and attribution reference all resolve to the same run_id |

**Assertions**

- the sandbox provider holds exactly one message for the effect_key and its receipt resolves in the sandbox provider API
- the suppressed sandbox identity produced zero provider calls and no provider id was manufactured for it — a denied action has no provider receipt to show: the case records the decision, the zero-call sink and the audit entry, and never presents a receipt, order id or message id the provider did not return
- the sandbox floor verdict, not local arithmetic, is what blocked the reduced price, and the offer that was sent respects the sandbox floor
- the recovered sandbox order resolves against the sandbox commerce API with the attributed amount, so the pilot passes on the conversion chain rather than on the send count

**Forbidden**

- sending to any address outside the approved sandbox allowlist
- reporting cart recovery from a sandbox queue acknowledgement instead of the provider receipt and the recovered order

**Evidence to collect (redacted)**

- sandbox provider message id plus the consent rows read at send time
- sandbox pricing-service verdict for the refused discount and the provider test-sink log (0 calls)
- sandbox order/receipt record for the recovered cart and the attribution reference (retained)

**Cleanup**

- Retire the sandbox artefacts created by this run through the supported sandbox APIs (cancel/withdraw the created cart, campaign, case and voucher references); delete nothing immutable — sent messages, provider receipts and audit rows are retained and reported as non-deletable rather than pretending they were unsent

**Automation seam.** Real code under test: skill registry row, authority guard/PEP, input validator, deadline and retry loop, effect_key reservation + reconciliation, evidence/audit writer. Substituted boundary: the external adapter (in-memory for offline, approved sandbox for live). Frozen clock 2026-01-15T10:00:00Z; all waits are condition/deadline waits on the engine's virtual clock, never sleep. Same flow over the sandbox commerce API with a single approved sandbox recipient and a sandbox-only cart.

**Prerequisites**

- ASM-001 approved connector lock is present (LIVE_CONNECTORS_LOCK points at the approved connector list) — without it this case is SKIP_ASM_001, never PASS
- Per-case sandbox authorization: the run_id of this case is registered in the approved sandbox allowlist with its sandbox tenant/customer/SKU mapping before execution; credentials live outside the repository (env.local) and are never printed in evidence

### `E2E-LIVE-CONNFAIL` - TC-E2E-008: connector 504/500 exhaustion, reconciliation and one real success (approved sandbox)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Suite | `e2e/live.md` |
| Layer | e2e |
| Environment | live |
| Priority | critical |
| Gate | P0 |
| Basis | blueprint |
| Pair | `E2E-OFF-CONNFAIL` |
| Source module | `sources/business.py` |
| Design status | `NOT_RUN` |

**Provenance**

- `TC-E2E-008` - A connector failure becomes failure/retry and never a fake success (SRS section 22)
- `NFR-004` - Availability: important workflows have retry, timeout and recovery (SRS section 19)
- `NFR-008` - Failure safety: when price, stock, authority or consent cannot be verified the system fails closed (SRS section 19 (MUST))
- `BR-006` - Retry must not create a duplicate action (SRS section 13 (MUST))
- `BR-010` - Every important execution must produce evidence (SRS section 13 (MUST))
- `NFR-002` - Auditability: 100% of externally changing actions carry an audit/evidence record (SRS section 19 (MUST))
- `NFR-005` - Explainability: important decisions store reason and evidence (SRS section 19)
- `SRS-09` - Revenue Orchestrator: central coordination and the eleven-stage lifecycle SIGNAL..LEARNING (SRS section 9)

**Real-life risk.** A flaky upstream connector is recorded as a success (or blindly retried) so the customer is told an order exists that the ERP never created — or is charged twice.

**Coverage facets**

- `skill:skill.sales.create_order` - skill.sales.create_order [skill, SRS section 11] (requires SAL-02)
- `event:checkout` - checkout [event, SRS section 15] (requires API-002)

- `stage:OUTCOME` - OUTCOME [stage, SRS section 9] (requires FR-ORC-002, SRS-09)
- `kpi:Failed Execution` - Failed Execution [kpi, AI System, SRS section 20]
- `kpi:Duplicate Execution` - Duplicate Execution [kpi, AI System, SRS section 20]

**Preconditions**

1. run_id=RUN-E2E-LIVE-CONNFAIL, case_id=E2E-LIVE-CONNFAIL, worker=w-biz-e2e-live; the sandbox order is created for the sandbox customer with the sandbox SKU and a sandbox-only amount
2. the sandbox provider account is a dedicated test account so the order count for the effect_key is observable through the sandbox API

**Inputs** (synthetic test configuration, never production policy)

```json
{
  "tenant_id": "LIVE_TENANT_ID",
  "customer_id": "LIVE_CUSTOMER_A_SANDBOX_ID",
  "sku_id": "LIVE_SKU_OK",
  "skill_id": "skill.sales.create_order",
  "effect_key": "EK-E2E-LIVE-CONNFAIL-<run_id>",
  "request_id": "sandbox inbound event id",
  "connector_fault_matrix": "sandbox-injected timeout/5xx then success",
  "sandbox_amount": "sandbox-only amount"
}
```

**Steps**

| # | Action | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Inject the sandbox fault and take the first failure | the first sandbox attempt fails with the injected timeout/5xx and is persisted as a failed attempt carrying the injected status, never as a success |
| 2 | Exhaust the sandbox retry budget | the remaining budget is consumed honestly, the failure reaches the operator surface, and no sandbox order is reported |
| 3 | Reconcile against the sandbox provider | the lookup by effect_key returns no order, the reservation is released, and the reconciliation is recorded with its own entry |
| 4 | Resume and create the real sandbox order | the resumed attempt produces exactly one sandbox order whose id is returned by the sandbox API, and the reservation settles once |
| 5 | Replay the live request | the replay returns the stored receipt and the sandbox order count for the effect_key stays 1 |
| 6 | Verify fault-injection did not leak a false success | the sandbox provider test sink and the audit trail agree: one order, three attempts, and zero fabricated order ids for the failed attempts — a denied action has no provider receipt to show: the case records the decision, the zero-call sink and the audit entry, and never presents a receipt, order id or message id the provider did not return |

**Assertions**

- the sandbox provider holds exactly one order for the effect_key and its id equals the receipt the engine returned
- the failed attempts resolve to persisted entries with the injected upstream status and no order id
- the sandbox reconciliation lookup, not an in-process HTTP result, decided that the effect was absent before the resume
- the exhausted-budget path surfaced the injected failure to the operator instead of silently retrying beyond the declared budget

**Forbidden**

- creating a second sandbox order for the same inbound request
- treating a sandbox HTTP 200 without a provider order record as delivery

**Evidence to collect (redacted)**

- sandbox provider order record for the effect_key plus its id
- sandbox per-attempt audit entries with the injected upstream statuses
- provider test-sink call log for the failed attempts (no order created) and the operator notification (retained)

**Cleanup**

- Retire the sandbox artefacts created by this run through the supported sandbox APIs (cancel/withdraw the created cart, campaign, case and voucher references); delete nothing immutable — sent messages, provider receipts and audit rows are retained and reported as non-deletable rather than pretending they were unsent

**Automation seam.** Real code under test: skill registry row, authority guard/PEP, input validator, deadline and retry loop, effect_key reservation + reconciliation, evidence/audit writer. Substituted boundary: the external adapter (in-memory for offline, approved sandbox for live). Frozen clock 2026-01-15T10:00:00Z; all waits are condition/deadline waits on the engine's virtual clock, never sleep. Same components with sandbox fault injection; the sandbox provider receipt, not the HTTP result, decides success.

**Prerequisites**

- ASM-001 approved connector lock is present (LIVE_CONNECTORS_LOCK points at the approved connector list) — without it this case is SKIP_ASM_001, never PASS
- Per-case sandbox authorization: the run_id of this case is registered in the approved sandbox allowlist with its sandbox tenant/customer/SKU mapping before execution; credentials live outside the repository (env.local) and are never printed in evidence
- The sandbox ordering endpoint can be fault-injected through the approved sandbox facility and supports lookup by effect_key; if fault injection is unsupported the retry matrix sub-step is BLOCKED_PREREQUISITE, never PASS

<a id="case-e2e-live-p5-autonomy"></a>

### `E2E-LIVE-P5-AUTONOMY` - P5: controlled autonomy promotes low-risk work and still gates high risk (approved sandbox)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Suite | `e2e/live.md` |
| Layer | e2e |
| Environment | live |
| Priority | high |
| Gate | P5 |
| Basis | blueprint |
| Pair | `E2E-OFF-P5-AUTONOMY` |
| Source module | `sources/business.py` |
| Design status | `NOT_RUN` |

**Provenance**

- `AUTH-2` - Draft: create draft content or action (SRS section 12)
- `AUTH-3` - Bounded Execute: execute within an approved scope (SRS section 12)
- `AUTH-4` - Approval Required: prepare the action, a human approval is required (SRS section 12)
- `BR-007` - Financial or high-risk actions require approval (SRS section 13 (MUST))
- `BR-008` - An agent must not exceed its authority even when the LLM asks (SRS section 13 (MUST))
- `BR-009` - Customer-supplied prompt or content cannot raise agent authority (SRS section 13 (MUST))
- `NFR-001` - Security: agents reach data and tools only under authority; no test case may allow crossing an authority boundary (SRS section 19 (MUST))
- `NFR-005` - Explainability: important decisions store reason and evidence (SRS section 19)
- `NFR-007` - Human override: a human can pause or take over a workflow (SRS section 19)
- `BR-010` - Every important execution must produce evidence (SRS section 13 (MUST))

**Real-life risk.** Controlled autonomy is either cosmetic (nothing is ever promoted, so the platform stays manual) or unsafe: a high-risk refund or broadcast executes itself because the tenant sat in a higher autonomy mode with no promotion decision recorded.

**Coverage facets**

- `skill:skill.sales.send_message` - skill.sales.send_message [skill, SRS section 11] (requires SAL-02)
- `skill:skill.care.issue_retention_offer` - skill.care.issue_retention_offer [skill, SRS section 11] (requires CS-02)
- `channel:EMAIL` - EMAIL [channel, SRS section 15] (requires API-003)
- `stage:DECISION` - DECISION [stage, SRS section 9] (requires FR-ORC-002, SRS-09)
- `stage:PLAN` - PLAN [stage, SRS section 9] (requires FR-ORC-002, SRS-09)
- `stage:APPROVAL` - APPROVAL [stage, SRS section 9] (requires FR-ORC-002, SRS-09)
- `stage:EXECUTION` - EXECUTION [stage, SRS section 9] (requires FR-ORC-002, SRS-09)
- `memory:Agent Operational Memory` - Agent Operational Memory [memory, SRS section 16]
- `kpi:Autonomous Completion Rate` - Autonomous Completion Rate [kpi, AI System, SRS section 20]
- `kpi:Human Override Rate` - Human Override Rate [kpi, AI System, SRS section 20]

**Preconditions**

1. run_id=RUN-E2E-LIVE-P5, case_id=E2E-LIVE-P5, worker=w-biz-e2e-live; the sandbox tenant is configured for the promotion mode with one approved sandbox recipient and the sandbox channel is allowlisted
2. the sandbox approval queue and the sandbox operator pause control are reachable through the approved operator API for this run

**Inputs** (synthetic test configuration, never production policy)

```json
{
  "tenant_id": "LIVE_TENANT_ID",
  "customer_id": "LIVE_CUSTOMER_A_SANDBOX_ID",
  "channel": "EMAIL",
  "assigned_authority": "AUTH-3",
  "low_risk_action": "sandbox reorder reminder for LIVE_SKU_OK",
  "high_risk_action": "sandbox compensation above the unset threshold",
  "pause_probe": "sandbox operator pause of tenant autonomy",
  "sandbox_recipient": "approved test mailbox only"
}
```

**Steps**

| # | Action | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Promote and execute the low-risk sandbox action | the sandbox run records recommend -> draft -> auto-execute with the policy parameters and the sandbox provider returns a real receipt for the single send |
| 2 | Probe the high-risk sandbox action | the sandbox approval row is PENDING, no sandbox dispatch happens and the provider test sink logs 0 calls for it — the provider test sink is the oracle for every denied or refused step: its call log for the run stays empty, no provider id is manufactured for the attempt, and the audit entry records the refusal instead |
| 3 | Attempt the sandbox self-promotion | the prompt-text claim changes no sandbox promotion or authority state, and the attempt is recorded |
| 4 | Pause autonomy on the sandbox | the operator pause takes effect: the next low-risk sandbox action parks as a draft and no sandbox provider call is made for it |
| 5 | Restore autonomy on the sandbox | the next in-policy low-risk action auto-executes with a sandbox provider receipt, while a fresh high-risk action still gates on approval |
| 6 | Collect the live promotion and gate evidence | the sandbox promotion log, the pending high-risk approval and the pause record are tied to the run and retained |

**Assertions**

- the sandbox promotion log documents each autonomous execution with its criterion and the sandbox policy parameters used
- the high-risk sandbox action produced zero provider calls and no receipt while the approval was PENDING — a denied action has no provider receipt to show: the case records the decision, the zero-call sink and the audit entry, and never presents a receipt, order id or message id the provider did not return
- the sandbox pause measurably stopped auto-execution and the resume measurably restored it for eligible low-risk work
- no sandbox authority or promotion value changed from prompt text, and the audit trail records the attempt

**Forbidden**

- executing a high-risk sandbox action without the sandbox approval decision
- claiming the pause works from the absence of a provider call alone, without the parked-draft record and the operator pause entry

**Evidence to collect (redacted)**

- sandbox promotion decision log with criterion, parameters and eligibility
- sandbox high-risk approval row (PENDING) plus the provider test-sink log (zero calls)
- sandbox operator pause entry and the resumed action's receipt (retained)

**Cleanup**

- Retire the sandbox artefacts created by this run through the supported sandbox APIs (cancel/withdraw the created cart, campaign, case and voucher references); delete nothing immutable — sent messages, provider receipts and audit rows are retained and reported as non-deletable rather than pretending they were unsent

**Automation seam.** Real code under test: skill registry row, authority guard/PEP, input validator, deadline and retry loop, effect_key reservation + reconciliation, evidence/audit writer. Substituted boundary: the external adapter (in-memory for offline, approved sandbox for live). Frozen clock 2026-01-15T10:00:00Z; all waits are condition/deadline waits on the engine's virtual clock, never sleep. Same components against the sandbox, with the sandbox tenant autonomy configuration and the sandbox operator pause control.

**Prerequisites**

- ASM-001 approved connector lock is present (LIVE_CONNECTORS_LOCK points at the approved connector list) — without it this case is SKIP_ASM_001, never PASS
- Per-case sandbox authorization: the run_id of this case is registered in the approved sandbox allowlist with its sandbox tenant/customer/SKU mapping before execution; credentials live outside the repository (env.local) and are never printed in evidence
- The sandbox supports the tenant autonomy configuration and an operator pause control for the run; if either is unsupported the corresponding sub-step is BLOCKED_PREREQUISITE and the run reports it instead of assuming the behaviour
- No approved policy parameter exists for autonomous compensation amounts (ASM-004), so the high-risk probe must travel the approval route

2. a sandbox-only SKU is kept without any price record so the refusal path can be exercised on live data

**Inputs** (synthetic test configuration, never production policy)

```json
{
  "tenant_id": "LIVE_TENANT_ID",
  "sku_id": "LIVE_SKU_OK",
  "customer_id": "LIVE_CUSTOMER_A_SANDBOX_ID",

}
```

**Steps**

| # | Action | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Ask for the price of the sandbox SKU with no price record | the refusal is explicit with no number and the sandbox ERP confirms no price row |
| 2 | Ask for the sandbox SKU-OK price | the spoken price equals the sandbox ERP current price and the quote token is signed by the sandbox service |
| 3 | Stage the sandbox price change and re-ask | the refreshed value is picked up and the previous quote is not reused |
| 4 | Attempt the below-floor discount | the sandbox pricing service returns discount_allowed=false and no reduced price is spoken |
| 5 | Try the stale quote against the sandbox order path | the sandbox order path refuses before creating an order; the sandbox order list for this run stays empty |
| 6 | Collect the sandbox pricing evidence | every value observed in the dialogue maps to a sandbox ERP response captured during the run, the sandbox refusals are recorded, and no stale quote remains redeemable on the sandbox |

**Assertions**

- the spoken prices equal the sandbox ERP values observed during the run and the no-price SKU produces no number
- the stale quote cannot create an order: the sandbox order list for the run is empty and no order id is reported
- the discount refusal is visible as a pricing-service verdict rather than prose-only behaviour
- no price or discount value appears in the transcript without a sandbox ERP response behind it

**Forbidden**

- quoting a sandbox price the ERP did not publish
- creating an order at a stale or unauthorised price

- Per-case sandbox authorization: the run_id of this case is registered in the approved sandbox allowlist with its sandbox tenant/customer/SKU mapping before execution; credentials live outside the repository (env.local) and are never printed in evidence

### `E2E-LIVE-TRACE` - TC-E2E-009: backward audit traceability from outcome to originating signal (approved sandbox)

**Provenance**

- `TC-E2E-009` - Every successful action traces back Trigger, Context, Decision, Approval, Execution, Evidence, Outcome (SRS section 22)
- `NFR-002` - Auditability: 100% of externally changing actions carry an audit/evidence record (SRS section 19 (MUST))
- `NFR-005` - Explainability: important decisions store reason and evidence (SRS section 19)
- `BR-010` - Every important execution must produce evidence (SRS section 13 (MUST))
- `FR-ORC-001` - Routing decides which agent handles, which skill is used, which data is accessed, which tool is called and whether approval is needed (SRS section 9 (MUST))
- `OBJ-005` - Orchestration: agents cooperate through workflows instead of acting independently (SRS section 1)
- `SRS-17` - Observability and audit: minimum Agent Run record fields (SRS section 17)
- `SRS-09` - Revenue Orchestrator: central coordination and the eleven-stage lifecycle SIGNAL..LEARNING (SRS section 9)

**Real-life risk.** Nobody can explain a completed customer-visible action: the audit trail is assembled from memory, a link is missing, or a tampered evidence row is accepted as proof.

**Coverage facets**

- `skill:skill.sales.create_order` - skill.sales.create_order [skill, SRS section 11] (requires SAL-02)
- `event:purchase` - purchase [event, SRS section 15] (requires API-002)
- `stage:SIGNAL` - SIGNAL [stage, SRS section 9] (requires FR-ORC-002, SRS-09)

- `stage:EXECUTION` - EXECUTION [stage, SRS section 9] (requires FR-ORC-002, SRS-09)
- `stage:EVIDENCE` - EVIDENCE [stage, SRS section 9] (requires FR-ORC-002, SRS-09)
- `stage:OUTCOME` - OUTCOME [stage, SRS section 9] (requires FR-ORC-002, SRS-09)

**Preconditions**

1. run_id=RUN-E2E-LIVE-TRACE, case_id=E2E-LIVE-TRACE, worker=w-biz-e2e-live; one sandbox run that creates a real sandbox order/message is completed first
2. the sandbox audit export for that run is fetched read-only and the sandbox verification facility (or the documented hash fields) is available for the walk

**Inputs** (synthetic test configuration, never production policy)

```json
{
  "tenant_id": "LIVE_TENANT_ID",
  "customer_id": "LIVE_CUSTOMER_A_SANDBOX_ID",
  "origin_signal": "sandbox inbound event id",
  "order_ref": "sandbox order id",
  "audit_export": "read-only sandbox audit trail for the run",
  "negative_probe": "case-local copy of the chain with one tampered payload"
}
```

**Steps**

| # | Action | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Complete one sandbox run | the run completes against the sandbox and its sandbox order/message id is recorded with the run_id |
| 2 | Fetch the sandbox audit trail read-only | the export contains the run entries for signal, context, decision, authority verdict, execution, evidence and outcome, all carrying the same run_id |
| 3 | Walk the chain backward on live records | outcome -> evidence -> execution -> decision -> context -> signal resolves with the sandbox ids, ending at the sandbox inbound event id |
| 4 | Verify the live chain hashes | the sandbox hash fields or the sandbox verification endpoint confirm the chain for the run with no unchained entry |
| 5 | Probe a broken link without touching the sandbox | the case-local chain copy with one tampered payload fails verification and the broken link is reported, while the sandbox rows themselves are left untouched |
| 6 | Confirm nothing was reconstructed from memory | the walk is repeated from the exported rows alone and reproduces the identical chain, with the sandbox artefacts retained |

**Assertions**

- every live walk hop resolves to a sandbox audit row with the identical run_id and ends at the real sandbox signal id
- the live chain verifies with the sandbox hash fields and the failed link inside the case-local copy is detected rather than hidden
- no sandbox immutable audit row was modified or deleted by the probe — the provider test sink is the oracle for every denied or refused step: its call log for the run stays empty, no provider id is manufactured for the attempt, and the audit entry records the refusal instead (the probe performs no provider mutation)
- the live trace is reproducible from the export after the run, so the case passes on the persisted chain rather than on an in-session view

**Forbidden**

- mutating or deleting sandbox audit/evidence rows to exercise the negative probe
- reporting a complete live trace while a stage entry is missing from the sandbox audit export

**Evidence to collect (redacted)**

- read-only sandbox audit export for the run with row ids and hashes
- sandbox chain verification result plus the case-local broken-link report
- the sandbox order/message id that anchors the outcome end of the chain

**Cleanup**

- Retire the sandbox artefacts created by this run through the supported sandbox APIs (cancel/withdraw the created cart, campaign, case and voucher references); delete nothing immutable — sent messages, provider receipts and audit rows are retained and reported as non-deletable rather than pretending they were unsent

**Automation seam.** Real code under test: skill registry row, authority guard/PEP, input validator, deadline and retry loop, effect_key reservation + reconciliation, evidence/audit writer. Substituted boundary: the external adapter (in-memory for offline, approved sandbox for live). Frozen clock 2026-01-15T10:00:00Z; all waits are condition/deadline waits on the engine's virtual clock, never sleep. Same reader against the sandbox audit trail; the broken-link probe runs on the case's own chain copy so no sandbox row is mutated.

**Prerequisites**

- ASM-001 approved connector lock is present (LIVE_CONNECTORS_LOCK points at the approved connector list) — without it this case is SKIP_ASM_001, never PASS
- Per-case sandbox authorization: the run_id of this case is registered in the approved sandbox allowlist with its sandbox tenant/customer/SKU mapping before execution; credentials live outside the repository (env.local) and are never printed in evidence
- The sandbox audit trail is readable for the run (API or approved export) and exposes row hashes; without a readable audit trail the case is BLOCKED_PREREQUISITE and no PASS is claimed
- The broken-link probe uses the case's own chain copy; sandbox immutable audit rows are never modified
